segments.caption: This model predicts Bangalore flat prices with 99% accuracy.
And it's completely useless. Can you spot why?
One of its inputs was the stamp duty paid. Stamp duty is calculated from the sale price. So the model was secretly reading the answer.
Before the flat is sold, that number doesn't even exist.
Day 6 of 100 Days of Machine Learning: features, labels, and the 6 tests every good feature must pass.
First, the words. The label, also called the target, is what you want to predict: the price.
Features are the inputs the model uses to predict it: area, bedrooms, locality, age.
And check the label too. Asking price or sold price? Predict the wrong one and everything after is wrong.
Test 1: will you know it at prediction time?
Stamp duty, days on market, final negotiated discount: all known only after the sale. Using them is data leakage.
Rule: if you won't have it when you predict, it can't be a feature.
Test 2: is it actually related to the label?
Listing ID number, or the broker's phone number. With enough rows, the model finds fake patterns in pure noise.
Rule: there should be a real reason it affects the price.
Test 3: is it a duplicate?
Area in square feet and area in square metres are the same information twice. The model gets confused about which one matters.
Rule: keep one version of each piece of information.
Test 4: is it filled in enough?
Parking type is blank for 70% of flats. Filling in that much would be mostly guessing.
Rule: drop it, or keep just a has parking info flag.
Test 5: does it actually vary?
City equals Bangalore, in every single row. A column that never changes can't explain anything.
Rule: remove constant and almost constant columns.
Test 6: is it fair and legal?
Never use things like the owner's religion or caste, even if they seem to correlate. And watch for proxies that sneak them back in.
Rule: if you couldn't defend it in public, don't use it.
And remember, the best features are often built, not found. Build year becomes age. An address becomes distance to the nearest metro.
So, the 6 tests: available in time, related, not duplicate, filled in, varies, and fair.
Save this, and run every feature through it.
